newsitem.title: CHINA: China stock indices little changed, sentiment weak.
newsitem.headline: China stock indices little changed, sentiment weak.

text.p: China's stock markets closed little changed in slow trading on Thursday due to weak market sentiment with foreign currency B shares slightly up and domestic A shares slightly down, traders said.
The markets are still under pressure from the threat of further official measures to rein them in and investors are reluctant to build positions, they said.
In Shanghai, the B share index stocks reserved for foreign investors rose 0.121 points or 0.15 percent to 82.918 on volume of 15.1 million shares worth $8.9 million.
The A index of shares for domestic investors lost 8.252 points or 0.65 percent to 1,265.838 on volume of 268.5 million shares worth 3.4 billion yuan.
In Shenzhen, the B share index rallied 0.96 points or 0.68 percent to close at 143.32 on turnover of HK$73 million.
But the A share index gave up early gains and shed 1.83 points or 0.44 percent to 412.91 with turnover shrinking to 4.8 billion yuan from Wednesday's 7.2 billion yuan.
Traders said signs of over-selling after Wednesday's fall on the Shanghai B share market made some investors build positions on Thursday.
"The day's rise on the (Shanghai B share market) is purely a technical rebound," said one trader. "It did not indicate any change to market fundamentals."
"Despite today's rise, volume was thin with most investors reluctant to build positions," one broker said.
Beijing has ordered state banks to unwind their share positions starting within 10 sessions from last Friday, in the latest move to cool down the nation's intensely speculative stock markets.
"Banks are retreating from the A share market in which they had previously built heavy positions," a Shenzhen-based analyst at a foreign brokerage in Shenzhen said.
"This is going to put downward pressure on the market through next week until the sell-off stops," he said.
Both the A and B share indices ended sharply lower on Wednesday on panic selling fuelled by apprehension over possible further market-dampening measures, brokers said.
A string of anti-speculation measures, ranging from a huge 30 billion yuan new share quota for 1997 to the latest ban on banks from entering the equity markets, has dealt a heavy blow to investors.
"Concerns over possible new measures will prevent strong rises in the near future," an analyst at China Guotai Securities said.
A wait-and-see attitude is likely to dominate the market on Friday, brokers said.

On the Shanghai B share market, Shanghai Steel Tube Co was the star performer on speculative buying after losing 17 percent in the past two days, rising $0.010 or 7.35 percent to $0.146 on volume of 17,000 shares.
Shanghai Erfangji Co was the worst A share performer, losing 0.32 yuan or 6.53 percent to 4.58.
In Shenzhen, Shenzhen Health Mineral Water was the heaviest B share gainer with a rise of HK$0.27 or 8.36 percent to HK$3.50.
Tellus Machinery's A share lost 0.58 yuan or 6.05 percent to 9.01 yuan to become the session's weakest performing A share.
